issues.expected: The email input shows the leading Lucide Mail icon at 20px (icon map: Email -> Mail; Input/Text anatomy includes a leading icon; both approved Login compositions show it; the password input correctly shows its LockKeyhole icon).
issues.actual: The email input renders with no leading icon at every viewport. DOM check confirms no svg inside the email field wrapper (style-audit.json desktop.loginUnauthenticated.emailHasLeadingIcon=false); LoginPage.jsx/RegisterPage.jsx do not pass an icon to TextInput although the component supports it.
issues.reproduction: Open /login (or /register) at any viewport and compare the Email field with docs/design/approved/mobile-login.jpg.

issues.expected: Desktop login centers a single visible login card: width 440px, card padding 40px, on the page background (responsive-layout.md, Login/Desktop) - the approved desktop composition shows a distinct surface card with rounded corners around logo, heading, and form.
issues.actual: No card is rendered: .auth-card is transparent (background rgba(0,0,0,0), padding 0, no shadow/border) with max-width 400px, so the form sits directly on the page background at 400px instead of a 440px card with 40px padding.
issues.reproduction: Open /login at 1440x900; inspect .auth-card computed styles (see style-audit.json desktop.loginUnauthenticated.authCard).

issues.expected: Mobile (320-767px) login form width is capped at 350px (responsive-layout.md, Login/Mobile: 'Maximum form width: 350px').
issues.actual: The form is capped at 400px, so between roughly 440px and 767px viewports it renders wider than the 350px mobile maximum (measured 400px at a 600px viewport).
issues.reproduction: Open /login at a 600px-wide viewport and measure the form width (400px).

issues.expected: Page titles use the kit's Heading/Page text style: DM Serif Display 400, 28/36 (figma-build-spec text styles); approved compositions show the large serif page title on Budget and Insights.
issues.actual: Authenticated page titles (Budget, Spending insights, Edit budget) render at 20px/30px DM Serif Display - a size that is not in the kit type ramp for page headings (20px belongs to Inter Heading/Section). Login's 'Welcome back' correctly uses 32px Display/Medium.
issues.reproduction: Open /budget or /insights; inspect the h1 computed font-size (20px; style-audit.json mobile.budget.title / desktop equivalents).

issues.expected: Button/Primary anatomy places the optional leading icon inline before the label; the approved Budget compositions show '+ Add expense' on a single line.
issues.actual: The Add-expense button renders the Plus icon stacked above the label (two visual lines) at every viewport (320-1440).
issues.reproduction: Open /budget with data at any viewport and look at the Add expense button.

issues.expected: Month tabs are ordered July (current, left) then June (previous, right): Tabs/Month options are listed 'July, June' in the component inventory and both approved Insights compositions show July on the left.
issues.actual: Tabs render June on the left and July on the right (chronological order), reversing the approved order at every viewport.
issues.reproduction: Open /insights and compare the tab order with docs/design/approved/mobile-insights.jpg.

issues.expected: The donut keeps a minimum usable plot size next to its legend (component code intends a 128-200px donut; kit constraint: 'Charts: scale while preserving labels and a minimum usable plot area'; approved compositions show a prominent donut).
issues.actual: In the legend-beside-donut layout the SVG is flex-shrunk far below its 128px minimum: ~95px at 1440, ~90px at 768, and ~25px at 1024, where the chart (and its center text) is unreadable. Mobile stacked/two-up layouts (320/390) are unaffected.
issues.reproduction: Open /insights at 1024x800 (worst), 768x1024, or 1440x900 and observe the donut size in the 'Spending by category' share card.

issues.expected: Donut inner radius is approximately 45% of the outer radius (figma-build-spec, Chart construction), i.e. a thick ring as shown in the approved compositions.
issues.actual: The ring is drawn with stroke width 0.13 x size centered at r=0.37 x size, giving an inner radius of ~70% of the outer radius - roughly half the specified ring thickness at every size.
issues.reproduction: Open /insights at 320px (largest rendering) and compare ring thickness with the approved compositions; see DonutChart.jsx radius/strokeWidth constants.

issues.expected: The donut center is empty; totals appear in the hero and values in the legend (figma-build-spec: segment labels appear in a separate legend; both approved compositions show an empty donut center).
issues.actual: A center total ('8,420' + month) is rendered inside the donut - an addition not present in any source; it duplicates the hero total and becomes illegible when the donut shrinks (D-DES-007).
issues.reproduction: Open /insights at any viewport and look at the donut center.

issues.expected: Cash-flow x-axis labels remain legible and non-overlapping at the smallest supported widths (kit accessibility checklist: 'Maintain legible labels at the smallest supported width').
issues.actual: In the 390px two-up layout the three x-axis labels collide: 'Jul 16Jul 31' render with no separation, and on the June view 'Jun 1Jun 16un 30' overlap/clip. The stacked 320px layout is fine.
issues.reproduction: Open /insights at 390x844 and inspect the Cash flow trend x-axis; switch to June for the worst case.

issues.expected: Line-chart circular point markers appear on hover only (figma-build-spec, cash-flow line chart); approved compositions show clean lines without persistent markers.
issues.actual: Markers are always visible on both series at all seven sample points, at every viewport. (Keyboard-focusable tooltip targets can remain while visually hidden until hover/focus.)
issues.reproduction: Open /insights and observe the Cash flow trend without hovering.

issues.expected: With the deterministic demo seed, the cash-flow chart reproduces the kit's reference series (content.json cashFlow: July 600->8,420 and June 800->9,180 rising from a low start), matching the approved chart shape used for comparison.
issues.actual: The seed reproduces the kit's monthly and per-category totals but front-loads day 1 (rent 3,500 + savings 600), so the cumulative curve starts at ~4,100 on Jul 1 instead of 600 and the rendered shape differs materially from the kit series and approved composition. Rendering and math are correct for the data; only the seeded distribution deviates. The roadmap fixes totals only, so honoring the content.json intermediate points conflicts with no higher-priority source.
issues.reproduction: Seed with ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true npm run seed:demo, sign in as demo@example.com, open /insights, and compare the Jul 1 value (~4.1K) with content.json cashFlow.july[0]=600.

issues.expected: Budget category rows have a desktop hover state (component inventory, Budget / Category row properties: 'Hover state for desktop').
issues.actual: No hover treatment exists: hovering a row produces no visual change (screenshot identical to the resting state) and no .category-row:hover rule is defined.
issues.reproduction: Open /budget at 1440x900 and hover a category row; compare budget-1440-row-hover.png with budget-1440.png.

issues.expected: Normal-size text meets WCAG AA 4.5:1; the kit's accessibility checklist explicitly requires 'White text on blue buttons must be checked against the implementation blue', and the roadmap gates on the contrast checklist passing.
issues.actual: White 16px/600 labels on blue-500 (#5B86D6) measure 3.60:1 - below AA for normal text - on all primary buttons (Sign in, Add expense, Create budget, Save expense/budget, Try again) and the selected July tab. This is a kit-internal conflict (color-scheme mandates blue-500 primary actions) that the developer documented and left for design adjudication; an in-ramp remedy exists (blue-600 #476FB9 = 4.95:1, already the hover fill).
issues.reproduction: Open any screen with a primary button and compute the contrast of white on #5B86D6 (3.60:1); see the developer contrast audit.

issues.expected: The 14px 'Planned' summary label meets WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text (kit accessibility checklist; roadmap contrast gate).
issues.actual: The label uses yellow-700 (#927427) on the background (#FAF8F4) at 4.17:1 - a near miss. Yellow-700 is already the darkest yellow token (kit semantic: yellow = planned), so no in-palette value passes at 14px; passing options include a larger/bolder label (>=18.66px bold qualifies for the 3:1 large-text bar) or a neutral text color with a yellow marker. Kit-internal conflict documented by the developer and left for design adjudication.
issues.reproduction: Open /budget and compute the contrast of the Planned label (#927427 on #FAF8F4 = 4.17:1).

intentionalDifferences.description: Category progress values (99/101/105/103/39 with three 'over plan' rows) differ from the kit's progressPercent values (63/34/26/28/56) shown in the approved compositions.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The kit percentages are mathematically inconsistent with the kit's own July actuals: roadmap (higher priority) fixes planned=10,200, July actual=8,420 per the content.json category values, and defines progress = actual/planned (3,957/4,000=99%, 1,516/1,500=101%, 842/800=105%, 926/900=103%, 1,179/3,000=39%). Both datasets cannot be honored at once; the roadmap wins per docs/workflow/source-of-truth.md. Overspent rows use the roadmap-required icon+text treatment, never color alone.

intentionalDifferences.description: Donut Savings segment uses kit token blue-700 instead of the category's blue-500 (which Housing also uses).
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The kit maps both Housing and Savings to 'blue'; identical fills meet where the ring wraps and would be indistinguishable, defeating the kit's own rule against relying on a single undifferentiated encoding. blue-700 stays in the kit blue ramp, adjacent-segment separation was validated by the developer, and legend + hidden data table carry identity regardless. The approved screenshot's teal Savings legend dot is itself a screenshot inconsistency (kit maps Savings to blue).

intentionalDifferences.description: Desktop grid places the bar chart at 8 columns beside the 4-column donut with the cash-flow chart full-width below, instead of the approved desktop composition's full-width bar chart.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The structured responsive-layout spec (bar 8 / donut 4 / line 12) conflicts with the approved desktop composition; within the kit, docs/ outrank reference imagery, and approved screenshots rank below structured kit values per source-of-truth. Mobile matches the approved composition.

intentionalDifferences.description: Lucide Trash2 (expense delete) and TriangleAlert (overspent/warning) are used although the kit icon map does not list delete/warning glyphs.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The icon map has no entry for these required purposes (roadmap requires delete affordances and non-color overspending signals). Both icons are Lucide outline glyphs, satisfying the map's family/outline rules; this is a gap-filling extension, not a substitution of a mapped icon.

intentionalDifferences.description: Copy beyond content.json: register page strings, expense/plan-form labels and statuses, state/error/empty strings, 'View insights'/'Back to budget' navigation entries, chart titles for states the kit does not cover, and tooltip wording.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: content.json covers only Login/Budget/Insights happy-path strings; the roadmap requires these screens and states to exist. Extensions are voice-consistent, marked in client/src/lib/copy.js, and flagged by the developer for design reconciliation. No kit-supplied string was altered.

intentionalDifferences.description: The unselected month tab is neutral (white surface) rather than the approved composition's simultaneous blue+yellow filled pair.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The component inventory defines colors for the selected states only ('Selected July uses blue. Selected June uses yellow with near-black text'); filling both tabs at once would make the selection state indistinguishable. Structured kit values win over the screenshot inconsistency. Selected states match the kit exactly.

intentionalDifferences.description: Roadmap-required UI beyond the approved compositions: month navigation row, Recent expenses history with per-item delete, create/edit budget form, and the various loading/empty/error/session states.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: The roadmap (higher priority than the compositions) mandates month navigation, expense history/delete, plan editing, and full state coverage; the kit provides no compositions for them. They are built from kit tokens and components and sit below/around the approved composition without altering it.

intentionalDifferences.description: The mobile Budget header shows the logo instead of the back arrow visible in the approved mobile composition; Insights keeps the back arrow.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: Budget is the app's root screen (nothing to go back to); the kit's Budget screen composition lists only page heading + more menu, so the mockup's back arrow is a screenshot inconsistency. Insights, which has a parent screen, retains the approved back arrow.

intentionalDifferences.description: Contrast-driven token consumption swaps within the kit ramp: coral-700 error text/danger buttons/warning banners, blue-700 Income label, green-600 Available value, 19px/700 comparison amount in yellow-700; June bars carry a diagonal pattern and visible text summaries accompany each chart.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: Required by the kit's own accessibility checklist (AA contrast; never color alone; a text summary per chart) which outranks the reference imagery; tokens.css remains byte-identical to the kit and only which token a component consumes changed. Documented in the developer contrast audit.

intentionalDifferences.description: Cash-flow y-axis tops at 10K (not the approved composition's 15K) and only three of seven sample dates are labeled.
intentionalDifferences.rationale: content.json's series max is 9,180, so a 15K axis is inconsistent with the kit's own data; structured content wins. The 3-label axis matches the approved composition's own labeling density (Jul 1 / mid / Jul 31).

notes: Scope: full delivery review (Login, Budget, Insights + register and budget-form subviews) at 390x844 and 1440x900 references plus 320/768/1024 reflow, 200% zoom equivalence (720px viewport), keyboard focus, and reduced motion. Reviewed against the running production-style build (SERVE_CLIENT) with the guarded deterministic demo seed.

Passes worth recording: no horizontal scroll at 320px on any screen (scrollWidth=320 on Login/Budget/Insights, capture-summary.json); reduced-motion leaves zero animated elements (reduced-motion-audit.json); browser console clean of JS errors/warnings on every captured page (console-log.json - only expected 401/404/aborted-request network entries); focus rings visible; dialogs (bottom sheet <768 / centered card >=768) match the kit; 44x44 targets confirmed on icon buttons; skeleton/empty/error/validation/loading/overspent/zero-progress/no-comparison/session-expired states all present and coherent; tooltips show category, month, value, and units on keyboard focus; June-selected tab uses yellow with near-black text per the kit.
Functional behavior (calculations, routing, persistence, API correctness) is QA-owned and was not gated here; no functional blocker impeded visual review.

Budget desktop content: the spec's 'maximum width 960px' is implemented as a 960px container including the 64px page paddings (832px card). The spec wording is ambiguous; the rendered result is consistent and matches neither reading exactly worse than the other, so it is recorded as a note, not an issue.

June-view chart coloring (selected June renders its own series in blue as the current-view month, dashed) is outside kit scope - the kit designs only the July view; recorded for awareness, not judged.

Capture used temporary env overrides RATE_LIMIT_MAX/RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX because the default general limiter throttles automated capture; product code and defaults unchanged (see capture-summary.json captureNotes).

The developer-flagged items were adjudicated as follows: kit progressPercent inconsistency -> intentional (D-DES-INT-001); donut Savings blue-700 -> intentional (D-DES-INT-002); desktop insights grid per spec -> intentional (D-DES-INT-003); Trash2/TriangleAlert icons -> intentional (D-DES-INT-004); the two kit-inherited contrast misses -> defects D-DES-014 / D-DES-015 because the kit's own accessibility checklist and the roadmap's contrast gate outrank the color assignment, and in-ramp remedies exist.
